summary: The depolarizing bug fix is mathematically sound: for qubit isotropic/Choi states the corrected formula is `E_R = 1 - h(F)`, and because `2⊗2` PPT = SEP, `E_R^PPT = E_R` exactly. The new amplitude-damping maximization also matches the known degradable-channel quantum-capacity formula, and targeted dense-grid spot checks agree with the golden-section optimizer. The patch still fails review because it upgrades that `Q` formula into a theorem-level claim about two-way `K_D`, and it uses per-sift BB84/six-state lower bounds against per-use `E_R` upper bounds, which makes the reported “near closure” ratios and follow-on scientific claims invalid. I could not run `pytest` in this read-only sandbox because no writable temp directory was available, so verification here is from direct inspection plus targeted Python spot checks.

issues.description: The quantity implemented as `max_p[h2((1-γ)p)-h2(γp)]` is the degradable qubit amplitude-damping channel’s quantum capacity, and for degradable channels also the unassisted private classical capacity. The patch repeatedly upgrades it to the channel’s 'true K_D' and even says it is a theorem-level upper bound for 'ANY 2-way LOCC protocol'. That is not what the cited degradable-channel results establish. In this repo, `K_D` is used for two-way distillable key / secret-key capacity, and the cited literature only supports one-way or unassisted notions here, not the two-way quantity. As written, the hierarchy table, candidate-D wording, and the new function name/documentation all overclaim the theorem.
issues.suggestion: Rename the API and all downstream references to something like `quantum_capacity_amplitude_damping_degradable` (or explicitly `private_capacity_1way_...` if that is the intended notion), and rewrite the docs to say 'known `Q` / unassisted private-capacity formula in the degradable regime' rather than 'true `K_D`'. Remove the claim that it upper-bounds arbitrary two-way LOCC key rates unless you add a separate theorem proving that step. Sources supporting the weaker statement: Devetak 2005 on secret-key capacity with forward public communication (`https://research.ibm.com/publications/the-private-classical-capacity-and-quantum-capacity-of-a-quantum-channel`), Smith 2008 on degradable channels and unassisted private capacity (`https://research.ibm.com/publications/private-classical-capacity-with-a-symmetric-side-channel-and-its-application-to-quantum-cryptography`), and Preskill §10.18 on amplitude damping degradability and optimized one-shot coherent information (`https://www.preskill.caltech.edu/ph219/chap10_6A_2022.pdf`).

issues.description: These tables compare channel-level `E_R` (bits/use) against BB84/six-state values that are plainly per-sift formulas (`1-2h(e)` and `1-h(e)-e log2 3`), not the repo’s per-signal rates used elsewhere (`0.5*(1-2h(e))` for BB84 and `(1-h(e)-e log2 3)/3` for six-state). That unit mismatch is why the docs report six-state as only `1.02x` to `1.79x` below the upper bound and call it 'near closure'. Using the repo’s actual per-signal convention, the six-state ratio is about `3.05x` at 1% QBER and about `5.37x` at 12.62% QBER, so the '≤1.8x' headline is not numerically valid. The follow-on inference that BB84’s specific EC term is the identified source of slack is also unsupported by this comparison.
issues.suggestion: Recompute every BB84/six-state table in per-signal units using the same convention as `qkdx/analytic/shor_preskill.py`, `qkdx/analytic/six_state.py`, and `qkdx/sweeps/bb84_family_sweep.py`, or explicitly relabel the lower bounds as per-sift and stop comparing them directly to per-use channel upper bounds. After fixing the units, downgrade 'near closure' and 'BB84 EC cost is non-tight' to conjectural observations unless you add a separate argument isolating those conclusions.

issues.description: The new optimizer relies on the concavity/unimodality of `I_c(p)` for `γ < 1/2`, but the tests do not verify the optimizer against a brute-force oracle and do not add out-of-range coverage for the new API. Current tests only check monotonicity/boundaries and the inequality against log-negativity, so a future regression in the search logic could still pass.
issues.suggestion: Add a small deterministic regression that compares `K_D_amplitude_damping_degradable(g)` against a dense-grid maximum for a few `g` values, especially near `g=0.49`, and extend `test_invalid_parameter_raises` to include the new function.

round_recommendation: Round 2 FIX: 1) rename/re-scope the AD function and all docs from `K_D` to `Q`/unassisted private capacity, removing the unsupported two-way-LOCC theorem language; 2) recompute the BB84/six-state comparison tables in per-signal units and delete or downgrade the 'near closure' / 'EC-cost' claims; 3) add a brute-force optimizer regression and invalid-input coverage for the new function. Then re-run review.
